title: Optical Illusions
definition: An optical illusion is characterized by visually perceived images that differ from objective reality, arising due to physiological mechanisms of the human visual system or cognitive misinterpretations of sensory inputs.
importanceInUpsc: Tested frequently in UPSC Prelims under Science and Technology (Physics/Biology overlapping concepts like total internal reflection, refraction, and human eye anatomy) and in Mains GS-3 for applications of science in daily life and cognitive phenomena.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Optical Illusions.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Basic geometric optics (reflection, refraction, total internal reflection)
Human eye anatomy and neural processing
